candidate.answerReason: The even power ends in 25, so subtracting 2017 produces final digits 08. Its tens digit is 0, agreeing with choice A.

methods.label: Track only the last two digits
methods.explanation:
To find a tens digit, it is enough to track the last two digits. In a product, digits farther left contribute multiples of \(100\), so only the last two digits of each factor affect the final two digits.

Since \(15^2=225\), the number \(2015^2\) ends in \(25\). Also, \(25\cdot25=625\), so multiplying two numbers ending in \(25\) gives another number ending in \(25\). Repeated multiplication therefore preserves this ending.

The exponent is even, and
\[
2015^{2016}=(2015^2)^{1008}.
\]
This is a product of \(1008\) factors ending in \(25\), so it too ends in \(25\). Subtracting \(2017=2000+17\) removes whole hundreds and then changes the ending from \(25\) to \(25-17=8\). The final two digits are \(08\), so the tens digit is \(0\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution proves a last-two-digit multiplication pattern using place value and grouping an even number of factors.
